an5276_topology: RFO1 -> L_EMC1 -> node A1 -> Cs1 -> node B1 -> R1 -> ANT2 -> antenna
RFO2 -> L_EMC2 -> node A2 -> Cs2 -> node B2 -> R2 -> ANT1 -> antenna
C_EMC1: A1 -> GND        C_EMC2: A2 -> GND
Cp1:    B1 -> GND        Cp2:    B2 -> GND
C_RFI_1/2 divider taps B1 to RFI1; C_RFI_3/4 taps B2 to RFI2

aqroot_as_built.aqroot: C69+C73 on NFC_EMCA, C70+C74 on NFC_EMCB
aqroot_as_built.note: two parts in parallel per arm to reach the value
NFC_MATCH_A carries exactly C71.2 and R114.1; NFC_MATCH_B exactly C72.2 and R115.1. THIS IS THE GAP THE REVIEW NAMED AND IT IS REAL.

aqroot_as_built.an5276: R1 / R2 (series damping to the antenna)
aqroot_as_built.note: the CTO addendum read AN5276's RQ -- a PARALLEL Q-adjust resistor discussed in section 4 -- as the topology element.  Figure 2 shows R1/R2 IN SERIES between the matching node and the antenna, which is exactly what R114/R115 are.  The series damping resistors are NOT a deviation.

AQROOT taps the receive divider AFTER R114/R115, at the antenna, where AN5276 taps it at node B before them.  The consequence is that the divider's own capacitance sits at the antenna node rather than at the matching node, so it does not substitute for Cp.

finding: ONE element of the AN5276 differential topology is absent: the parallel matching capacitor Cp.  Its VALUE cannot be derived here -- AN5276 derives Cs and Cp from the MEASURED antenna equivalent circuit (L_ANT, R_P@fres, C_ANT) with the ST25R antenna matching tool, and this antenna has not been built or measured -- so no component can be baselined and no value can be put on a BOM.
fit_notes: 0.325 mm is the EDGE-to-EDGE gap and the two arms agree to the last digit: mirror-exact.
an 0402 is 1.0 x 0.5 mm, so it bridges 0.325 mm with about 0.34 mm of overlap at each end.

both GND targets are PLATED BARRELS that the fab notes already instruct to fill and cap-plate -- 'applying the process to every via on the board is acceptable and is the simpler instruction' -- so each presents a planar, solderable land rather than an open hole.
no solder mask is removed, no track is cut, and the symmetry the RF1-RF5 contract protects is untouched because the two fits are geometric mirrors.
question: external first-spin review item 6 / CTO corroboration addendum: reconstruct the ST25R3916 matching network against the CURRENT ST application note and decide whether dedicated parallel tune positions must be added
residual: the tune remains a FIRST-ARTICLE activity, as it must be: AN5276 derives Cs and Cp from the measured antenna, and the antenna does not exist yet.  What D-755 changes is that the fit is now a MEASURED 0.325 mm pad-to-via bridge on both arms instead of an unquantified bodge, and that the comparison against the note is on the record.

resolution.action: NO BOARD CHANGE.  Record the fit; do not re-floorplan the front end.
resolution.fit: AND IT DOES NOT HAVE TO BE A REWORK.  D-751 recorded the tune element as 'an ordinary 0402 tacked across a measured 0.500 mm gap' to B.Cu GND FILL, which would mean removing solder mask.  The real geometry is better and is measured here: on each arm the matching node's own SOLDER PAD faces a GND VIA at the same x, and the two arms are EXACT MIRRORS about y = 30.000.
resolution.why: adding dedicated Cp positions means re-floorplanning the most symmetry-critical region on the board.  The outboard rows either side of the matching nodes are FULL -- y = 25.700 carries C73, R116 and C76, and y = 34.300 their exact mirrors C74, R117 and C78 -- and the inboard space carries the NFC_RFI1/RFI2 runs and their barrels.  There is no symmetric site.  Spending the RF1-RF5 symmetry budget, the D-224 circular antenna geometry and the pour partition to add two DNP pads whose NEED is unproven until the antenna is measured is a bad trade on a first spin.
